_: Clear front shell of the eye: epithelium (~50 um), Bowman, collagen stroma (~90 %), Descemet, endothelium; 0.53-0.55 mm thick at the centre, R 7.8 mm front, held taut by intraocular pressure and always wet with the tear film. Adult, ~34 C surface, IOP ~15 mmHg. Eye-and-hair materials lane, 2026-11-07.

alpha.src: the tear film is a free liquid surface (tears.json alpha 0.003, water 0.005): the cornea's highlight is mirror-sharp; a broken film roughens it (states)

n.src: EYEMD G1 bulk cornea 1.376 (epithelium 1.401, stroma 1.373-1.380); the outer surface optically is the tear film 1.337

absorption.v: clear in the visible; transmits > ~90 % from ~450 nm, absorbs UV below ~300 nm

scattering.v: very weak (lattice-ordered collagen fibrils); haze rises when swollen
scattering.src: textbook transparency theory, not measured here

kinetic.src: CHEN26 (porcine lid on eyeball 0.05 +/- 0.01); WILSON15 human cornea vs mucin glass; MORRISON12 human cornea vs PDMS; Barros 2015 pig cornea vs glass (via CHEN26)

friction.counterface: eyelid (lid wiper) with tear film; glass and PDMS stand-ins listed for comparison

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: not found: the glycocalyx (membrane mucins) makes the epithelium hydrophilic and anti-adhesive (CHEN26 discussion)

tack.v: none while the glycocalyx is intact; dry patches stick (bare-glass mu_s 2.1 shows what the mucin layer prevents)

restitution.src: not found; a soft wet shell: impacts are absorbed by the pressurised globe (see solver)

water_contact_angle_deg.src: not found as a number; healthy epithelium is fully wetted by tears (film breakup > 10 s, tears.json)

blink_speed_mm_s.src: EYEMD I3 (Kwon 2013, mean speeds); LIEVENS22 average 12 cm/s

water_absorption.v: stroma ~78 % water, kept dehydrated by the endothelial pump; swells (thickens, hazes) when the pump or epithelium fails
water_absorption.src: textbook hydration, recalled; E: recalled, not re-read

triboelectric.src: not found; wet tissue: charge leaks instantly

phase.src: a pressurised soft shell, always lubricated

collision_thickness_mm.src: the tear film's aqueous-mucin layer 3.3 um (EYEMD F1): the lid rides on it, never on the epithelium

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: E_stack / thickness: posterior-weighted stroma ~0.3 MPa (LOMBARDO14 0.17-0.21 back, 2.3 front; QIN21 Ogden mu 0.42-0.74) over 0.535 mm; porcine whole-eyeball indentation stiffness 0.1 MPa (CHEN26). At the scale of the whole eye the IOP carries the load (iop_support)

iop_support.v: Imbert-Fick: a flat contact of area A is held by F = IOP x A (Goldmann tonometry: 3.06 mm diameter at 1 g per 10 mmHg); press harder and the globe dents, aqueous is displaced against the ocular rigidity

ramp.src: IPC barrier at the tear-film thickness; friction from the pair table (lid on cornea ~0.05)

contact_damping_ratio.src: viscoelastic stroma (creep minutes, LOMBARDO14) plus the fluid-filled globe: heavily damped; no measured ratio

E_kPa.src: liquid: carries pressure, no shear stiffness

compressible_to_fraction.src: squeezed out sideways under the lid (it thins to the lid-wiper gap)

E_kPa.src: not found separately; LOMBARDO14's anterior value with vs without epithelium (2.28 vs 3.30 MPa) implies the epithelium is the softer skin

compressible_to_fraction.src: cells deform little before damage (CHEN26 wear depth 8-12 um)

E_kPa.src: a liquid: its 'stiffness' is the IOP (15.5 mmHg = 2.07 kPa) plus the globe's ocular rigidity (deform.iop)

poisson.src: incompressible; it moves, it does not compress

compressible_to_fraction.src: volume conserved: indentation pushes aqueous out to the rest of the globe, raising IOP

response_time_ms.src: Corvis ST air-puff deformation and recovery take ~20-30 ms (instrument record, recalled): the time a poke or blink impulse reads in; E: recalled, not re-read

model.src: fibre-reinforced (collagen lamellae) hyperelastic; an isotropic Ogden fit is the simple option

E_kPa.src: LOMBARDO14 (inflation 18-42 mmHg, human globes); in_vivo 0.29 MPa: RECALL Hamilton & Pye 2008 (not reopened, E strength)

ogden.src: QIN21 in vivo inverse fit (one-term Ogden)

anisotropy.v: in-plane lamellae: stiff in the plane, ~100x softer across (transverse shear); stiffer in the anterior third
anisotropy.src: NITI/OCE literature (arXiv 2006.10893 seen in search, not read) + LOMBARDO14 front-back gradient (M)

iop.src: RECALL population IOP (Colton & Ederer; not reopened); this is a world/state value carried by the globe, see eye.vitreous

v.law: log10 P2 - log10 P1 = K (V2 - V1)

strength_kPa.src: not found in a source read here

note.v: drive the shell with the IOP as a pressure load; the shape at rest is the pressurised one

surface_temperature_C.src: ocular surface thermography (recalled); SCOTT88 model with 20 C room; E: recalled, not re-read

dry_eye_breakup.src: breakup roughens the highlight (tears.json); friction rises toward the saline values (SCHMIDT13 mu_k 0.24-0.31 without lubricin) - 0.15 E

aged_60.src: cornea stiffens with age (Elsheikh 2007 inflation, recalled, not reopened); x1.4 E

EYEMD.cite: The project's research note eye.md (2026-10-19): A-I tables, G1 refractive indices, F1-F3 tear film, E1/E3/G5 sclera, C2 iris, D1-D3 lens, I3 blink
EYEMD.lic: project record; papers as cited there (R1-R69)

CHEN26.cite: Chen Y, Kaper HJ, de Jong E, van Kooten TG, Sharma PK. Importance of tribo-pairs to mimic blinking in vitro for dry eye disease research. Friction 14(8):9441241 (2026): porcine eyelid on eyeball, 30 mN, 8 mm/s: mu_s 0.16 +/- 0.04, mu_k 0.05 +/- 0.01; bare glass mu_s 2.10 +/- 0.60, mucin glass 0.59 +/- 0.19; tarsal plate 0.4 +/- 0.2 MPa, eyeball 0.1 +/- 0.08 MPa; Table 1 of literature values

WILSON15.cite: Wilson T, Aeschlimann R, Tosatti S et al. Coefficient of friction of human corneal tissue. Cornea 34(9):1179 (2015) (via CHEN26 Table 1): mucin-coated glass vs human cornea, 3.5-8.8 kPa, mean CoF 0.006-0.015 in tear-mimicking solutions
WILSON15.lic: paywalled; numbers via CHEN26 used as facts

SCHMIDT13.cite: Schmidt TA, Sullivan DA et al. JAMA Ophthalmol 131:766 (2013) (via CHEN26): human eyelid vs rabbit cornea, 15-20 kPa: saline mu_s 0.27-0.51, mu_k 0.24-0.31; PRG4 mu_s 0.14-0.29, mu_k 0.12-0.17

MORRISON12.cite: Morrison S, Sullivan DA, Sullivan BD, Sheardown H, Schmidt TA. Eye Contact Lens 38:27 (2012) (via CHEN26): PDMS vs human cornea 16.7 kPa, saline mu_s 0.29-0.37, mu_k 0.28-0.32

SHAW10.cite: Shaw AJ, Collins MJ, Davis BA, Carney LG. Eyelid pressure and contact with the ocular surface. IOVS 51:1911 (2010) (via CHEN26 Table 1: in vivo blink 1-10 kPa)
SHAW10.lic: IOVS (CC BY-NC-ND for recent issues; this one not checked): number used as fact

LIEVENS22.cite: Lievens CW, Rayborn E. Tribology and the ocular surface. Clin Ophthalmol 16:973 (2022): blink contact pressure 3.5-4.0 kPa (lens wearer), average blink speed 12 cm/s
LIEVENS22.lic: CC BY-NC 3.0: numbers used as facts, text studied only (P13)

LOMBARDO14.cite: Lombardo M et al. Analysis of the viscoelastic properties of the human cornea using Scheimpflug imaging in inflation experiment of eye globes. PLoS One 9:e112169 (2014): anterior E 2.28 +/- 0.87 MPa (epithelium on) / 3.30 +/- 0.90 (off); posterior 0.21 +/- 0.09 / 0.17 +/- 0.06 MPa; IOP 18-42 mmHg; Zener creep tau_load 5.50 min, tau_unload 1.10 min (anterior, epithelium on)

QIN21.cite: Exploring the biomechanical properties of the human cornea in vivo based on Corvis ST. Front Bioeng Biotechnol (2021) 10.3389/fbioe.2021.771763: Ogden mu 0.42-0.74 MPa, alpha 32.76-55.63 (inverse FE, in vivo)
QIN21.lic: CC BY 4.0 (numbers read via search summary)

SCOTT88.cite: Scott JA. A finite element model of heat transport in the human eye. Phys Med Biol 33:227 (1988), Table 1: cornea k 0.58, c 4178, rho 1050; aqueous 0.58 / 3997 / 1000; lens 0.40 / 3000 / 1050; vitreous 0.603 / 4178 / 1000; iris and ciliary as aqueous; corneal emissivity 0.975; tear evaporation 40-100 W/m2; h_air 10, h_blood 65 W/m2K
SCOTT88.lic: IOP paywalled; numbers used as facts

WILDE12.cite: Wilde GS, Burd HJ, Judge SJ. Shear modulus data for the human lens determined from a spinning lens test. Exp Eye Res 97:36 (2012), PMC3405528: Model D nucleus/cortex G at 33 y 0.19/0.93, 43 y 1.28/1.41, 50 y 7.35/1.16 kPa; age-stiffness fits GN (A* 27.5, b1 0.00562, b2 0.0767, c 68.8 Pa), GC (43.0, 0.0235, -0.00932, 1340 Pa); nucleus stiffer than cortex from ~45 y

HEYS04.cite: Heys KR, Cram SL, Truscott RJW. Massive increase in the stiffness of the human lens nucleus with age: the basis for presbyopia? Mol Vis 10:956 (2004): nucleus ~450x, cortex ~20x stiffer over life; young nucleus softer than cortex
HEYS04.lic: Mol Vis open access (CC BY-NC-ND per journal; ratios used as facts, P13)

TRAM18.cite: Tram NK, Swindle-Reilly KE. Rheological properties and age-related changes of the human vitreous humor. Front Bioeng Biotechnol 6:199 (2018) and erratum PMC6428972: human G' 6.5 +/- 3.0 Pa, G'' 0.96 +/- 0.47 Pa (n 23); porcine 5.0/0.65; literature table (Shafaie, Filas, Nickerson, Swindle E 57.3 Pa...)

GERAGHTY12.cite: Geraghty B, Jones SW, Rama P, Akhtar R, Elsheikh A. Age-related variations in the biomechanical properties of human sclera. J Mech Behav Biomed Mater 16:181 (2012): tangent modulus at 1 MPa / at 0.05 MPa = 11.2 / 12.0 / 12.4 (anterior / equator / posterior); stiffening with age; stiffness falls anterior to posterior
GERAGHTY12.lic: paywalled; ratios read in a search summary; used as facts
